punchline: A man could describe a glove perfectly without knowing it was a glove, yet he could dress himself as long as he was singing.
thirty_sec: Oliver Sacks's patient Dr. P. was a singer and music teacher whose eyes were fine. He took his own foot for his shoe, described a glove as a continuous surface with five outpouchings, and reached for his wife's head as if it were a hat. But with a song he could eat and dress, and he froze when it was interrupted. Sacks told him to make music the whole of his life.
